legend: Mike received an array a%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%% as a birthday present and decided to test how pretty it is.
An array would pass the i%%ZSMJ2%%-th prettiness test if there is a way to get an array with a sum of elements totaling si%%ZSMJ3%%, using some number (possibly zero) of slicing operations.
An array slicing operation is conducted in the following way:

assume mid=⌊max(array)+min(array)2⌋%%ZSMJ4%%, where max%%ZSMJ5%% and min%%ZSMJ6%% — are functions that find the maximum and the minimum array elements. In other words, mid%%ZSMJ7%% is the sum of the maximum and the minimum element of array%%ZSMJ8%% divided by 2%%ZSMJ9%% rounded down.

Then the array is split into two parts left%%ZSMJ10%% and right%%ZSMJ11%%. The left%%ZSMJ12%% array contains all elements which are less than or equal mid%%ZSMJ13%%, and the right%%ZSMJ14%% array contains all elements which are greater than mid%%ZSMJ15%%. Elements in left%%ZSMJ16%% and right%%ZSMJ17%% keep their relative order from array%%ZSMJ18%%.
During the third step we choose which of the left%%ZSMJ19%% and right%%ZSMJ20%% arrays we want to keep. The chosen array replaces the current one and the other is permanently discarded.
You need to help Mike find out the results of q%%ZSMJ21%% prettiness tests.

Note that you test the prettiness of the array a%%ZSMJ22%%, so you start each prettiness test with the primordial (initial) array a%%ZSMJ23%%. Thus, the first slice (if required) is always performed on the array a%%ZSMJ24%%.
input: Each test contains one or more test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ25%% (1≤t≤100%%ZSMJ26%%).
The first line of each test case contains two integers n%%ZSMJ27%% and q%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤n,q≤105)%%ZSMJ29%% — the length of the array a%%ZSMJ30%% and the total number of prettiness tests.
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ31%% integers a1,a2,...,an%%ZSMJ32%% (1≤ai≤106)%%ZSMJ33%% — the contents of the array a%%ZSMJ34%%.
Next q%%ZSMJ35%% lines of each test case contain a single integer si%%ZSMJ36%% (1≤si≤109)%%ZSMJ37%% — the sum of elements which Mike wants to get in the i%%ZSMJ38%%-th test.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ39%% and the sum of q%%ZSMJ40%% does not exceed 105%%ZSMJ41%% (∑n,∑q≤105%%ZSMJ42%%).
output: Print q%%ZSMJ43%% lines, each containing either a "Yes" if the corresponding prettiness test is passed and "No" in the opposite case.
note: Explanation of the first test case:

We can get an array with the sum s1=1%%ZSMJ44%% in the following way: 1.1 a=[1,2,3,4,5]%%ZSMJ45%%, mid=1+52=3%%ZSMJ46%%, left=[1,2,3]%%ZSMJ47%%, right=[4,5]%%ZSMJ48%%. We choose to keep the left%%ZSMJ49%% array.
 1.2 a=[1,2,3]%%ZSMJ50%%, mid=1+32=2%%ZSMJ51%%, left=[1,2]%%ZSMJ52%%, right=[3]%%ZSMJ53%%. We choose to keep the left%%ZSMJ54%% array.
 1.3 a=[1,2]%%ZSMJ55%%, mid=1+22=1%%ZSMJ56%%, left=[1]%%ZSMJ57%%, right=[2]%%ZSMJ58%%. We choose to keep the left%%ZSMJ59%% array with the sum equalling 1%%ZSMJ60%%.
It can be demonstrated that an array with the sum s2=8%%ZSMJ61%% is impossible to generate.

An array with the sum s3=9%%ZSMJ62%% can be generated in the following way: 3.1 a=[1,2,3,4,5]%%ZSMJ63%%, mid=1+52=3%%ZSMJ64%%, left=[1,2,3]%%ZSMJ65%%, right=[4,5]%%ZSMJ66%%. We choose to keep the right%%ZSMJ67%% array with the sum equalling 9%%ZSMJ68%%.
It can be demonstrated that an array with the sum s4=12%%ZSMJ69%% is impossible to generate.

We can get an array with the sum s5=6%%ZSMJ70%% in the following way: 5.1 a=[1,2,3,4,5]%%ZSMJ71%%, mid=1+52=3%%ZSMJ72%%, left=[1,2,3]%%ZSMJ73%%, right=[4,5]%%ZSMJ74%%. We choose to keep the left%%ZSMJ75%% with the sum equalling 6%%ZSMJ76%%.
Explanation of the second test case:
It can be demonstrated that an array with the sum s1=1%%ZSMJ77%% is imposssible to generate.

We can get an array with the sum s2=2%%ZSMJ78%% in the following way: 2.1 a=[3,1,3,1,3]%%ZSMJ79%%, mid=1+32=2%%ZSMJ80%%, left=[1,1]%%ZSMJ81%%, right=[3,3,3]%%ZSMJ82%%. We choose to keep the left%%ZSMJ83%% array with the sum equalling 2%%ZSMJ84%%.
It can be demonstrated that an array with the sum s3=3%%ZSMJ85%% is imposssible to generate.

We can get an array with the sum s4=9%%ZSMJ86%% in the following way: 4.1 a=[3,1,3,1,3]%%ZSMJ87%%, mid=1+32=2%%ZSMJ88%%, left=[1,1]%%ZSMJ89%%, right=[3,3,3]%%ZSMJ90%%. We choose to keep the right%%ZSMJ91%% array with the sum equalling 9%%ZSMJ92%%.
We can get an array with the sum s5=11%%ZSMJ93%% with zero slicing operations, because array sum is equal to 11%%ZSMJ94%%.
